problem:
Find the interval of convergence for the following series:

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{x}^{n}}{{4}^{n}(5n-2)}=\frac{x}{4\cdot 3}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{{4}^{2}\cdot 8}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{{4}^{3}\cdot 13}+⋯
$$

The interval of convergence is
{{field-1}}
$\le x$
{{field-2}}{{field-3}}.
worked_solution:
To apply the ratio test, we define ${a}_{n}=\frac{{x}^{n}}{{4}^{n}(5n-2)}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{x}^{n+1}}{{4}^{n+1}(5n+3)}\cdot \frac{{4}^{n}(5n-2)}{{x}^{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{x(5n-2)}{4(5n+3)}| \\  & =\frac{|x|}{4}{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{5n-2}{5n+3} \\  & =\frac{|x|}{4}\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{|x|}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{|x|}{4}<1\,⟹\,|x|<4.
$$

So, the radius of convergence is $4,$ and the series converges for any $x$ that lies in the open interval $(-4,4).$

The ratio test gives no conclusion about the convergence of the series when $L=1.$ So, when $|x|=4,$ we do not know if the series converges. This means that the endpoints $x=-4$ and $x=4$ need to be investigated separately using another test for convergence.

- When $x=4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{x}^{n}}{{4}^{n}(5n-2)} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{4}^{n}}{{4}^{n}(5n-2)} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{5n-2} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{8}+\frac{1}{13}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

To see if this series converges, we use the limit comparison test, with ${a}_{n}=\frac{1}{5n-2}$ and ${b}_{n}=\frac{1}{n}.$ We observe that ${a}_{n}$ and ${b}_{n}$ are positive, and

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{{a}_{n}}{{b}_{n}}={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{1}{5n-2})}{(\frac{1}{n})}={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{n}{5n-2}=\frac{1}{5},
$$

 
which is positive and finite. Hence, the series ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}$ and ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}$ either *both* converge or *both* diverge.
Since ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{n}$ is divergent, the series ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{5n-2}$ is also divergent by the limit comparison test. So, the endpoint $x=4$ is not included in our interval.

- When $x=-4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{x}^{n}}{{4}^{n}(5n-2)} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-4)^{n}}{{4}^{n}(5n-2)} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n}}{5n-2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{8}-\frac{1}{13}+⋯,\end{aligned}
$$

which is convergent by the alternating series test. So, the endpoint $x=-4$ is included in our interval.

Therefore, the interval of convergence is $[-4,4),$ or equivalently, $-4\le x<4.$
